compute.reported_as: Energy results achieved by wave-functions before and after a Lanczos step are evaluated with the MC sample number in the magnitude of O(4.5×10^4). [Sec. III] ... (1) With a sample size of O(4.5×10^4), the step size is initially set to 2×10^−3 and then reduced to 2×10^−4. (2) With a sample size of O(4.5×10^4), the step size is initially set to 2×10^−3, the sample size is then increased to O(4.5×10^5) while maintaining the step size, and finally, the step size is reduced to 2×10^−4. ... For lattices larger than 64 sites, both strategies require no more than 2×10^4 optimization steps to achieve full convergence. [Sec. III.A] ... X. Liang thanks Eric J. Walter for resource allocations on the William & Mary Sciclone cluster. The author acknowledges William & Mary Research Computing and the Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC) at The University of Texas at Austin for providing computational resources that have contributed to the results reported within this paper. Part of numerical results were obtained on the Bridges-2 at Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center through allocation (phy240244). [Sec. V Acknowledgement] || Sec. II.A (v4): "the final dimension of g is [12]: [M,N,Q,d,d], (4) where M denotes the number of sites, N is the total number of particles, and d represents the number of degrees of freedom at each site. ... Q =5 when backflow terms from nearest-neighbor sites are included, and Q = M when backflow terms from all sites are considered." || "The total number of variational parameters equals the product of the dimensions of all indices of g." || Sec. III.2: "According to Eq.( 4 ), for a filling of n =0.875 on 64-site lattices, the parameter numbers for NN and all-site backflow are 286,720 and 3,670,016, respectively. For the 16×16 lattice with NN backflow, the parameter number is 4,587,520." || Table 5 caption: "Energy results obtained by direct optimizations for n =0.875 and U =8." (rows 8×16, 8×24, 8×32, t′ = 0, Backflow Type NN)

III.2 and Table 3 (parameter numbers); Table 5 (backflow type of these rows), arXiv:2507.01856v4 (https://arxiv.org/html/2507.01856v4) (route2b-pass 2026-09-24) (compute pass 2026-09-24)
compute.note: No device, GPU/CPU count, wall-clock or core-hours stated anywhere (main text, Tables I-VII, Figs. 1-14 captions, Appendices A-D); the acknowledgement names the Sciclone, TACC and Bridges-2 clusters without quantities. samples = order-of-magnitude statement O(4.5×10^4) for energy evaluation (optimization used O(4.5e4) rising to O(4.5e5) in strategy 2; 46,080 samples are quoted for structure factors in App. B / Fig. 8). iterations = stated upper bound only: "no more than 2×10^4 optimization steps" for lattices larger than 64 sites (Sec. III.A); also "fewer than 2×10^4 optimization steps" for the Table II results. || route2b-pass 2026-09-24: parameters = M x N x Q x d x d = 256 x 224 x 5 x 4 x 4 = 4587520 (M = 256 sites, N = 224 electrons at n = 0.875, Q = 5 for NN backflow per Table 5, d = 4 local states). The formula reproduces the three counts the paper prints (286,720 and 3,670,016 on 64 sites, 4,587,520 on 16x16 NN), which also fixes d = 4. The count is lattice-size dependent (grows as M x N). The UHF-extended layout g[r_i, k sigma_k, sigma_i, 2, j, s(r_j)] used for direct optimization has the same product (16 M N Q). The p = 1 row has the same tensor; its Lanczos step (O(N^4 Q) per amplitude, O(N^5 Q) for the variance) is not counted by nqs-v1. Only the N x N x Q entries selected by a configuration are read per amplitude (250880 here), so the ARCH 'Tensor backflow' reuse = 1 overcounts the forward pass by M d^2 / N = 18.3x.
